response.explanation: Line 1 of src/domain/subscription.ts imports SystemClock from the outbound adapter src/adapters/outbound/system-clock.ts. Line 4 creates an instance of it, and isActive() on line 9 calls clock.now() to compare the current time with endsAt. The graph shows the same thing: a CALLS edge to SystemClock.now and a FLOWS_TO edge to the SystemClock class. FF-S04 flags this because a core (domain) file depends directly on a concrete adapter-layer file, so the core's dependency points outward rather than going through a port the core owns. That makes Subscription's time-dependent behaviour tied to the real system clock and hard to test or replace. The project chose to do this on purpose. ADR-0002 has status Accepted, says the domain core may import SystemClock from exactly this adapter file, and states that no Clock port will be added for now. The rule's verdict stands. The ADR records the reason the dependency exists, and its 'for now' wording means the decision is temporary.
